mainTopic: The husband's rights to produce of his wife's מלוג property: offspring, items that wear out, inherited old slaves and trees, and his spending on her property
overview: The amud opens with the end of רבי ינאי's ruling: a thief who steals the offspring of a wife's מלוג animal pays the כפל to the wife. The גמרא answers that the husband was given only פירא, not פירא דפירא, so everyone can agree. It then asks why the רבנן give a maidservant's child to the wife but an animal's offspring to the husband. The answer is that a dead animal still leaves its hide. שמואל rules like חנניה, and רב נחמן adds that a divorced wife may buy back her maidservant's children because of שבח בית אביה. רב נחמן also rules that items brought in for their produce, such as a goat, a hen, or a cloak, may be used until they are gone, following the חכמים about mines, and רבא explains how רבי שמעון differs from the תנא קמא. A new משנה deals with old slaves and old trees the wife inherits, and the גמרא reverses רב's limit on that dispute after רב יוסף's challenge. A final משנה covers a husband's spending on his wife's property, and רבי אסי says even one dried fig counts as 'a little'. The amud ends as a new statement begins, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The thief pays the double payment to the wife
steps.stepSummary: The end of רבי ינאי's ruling: someone who steals the offspring of a מלוג animal pays the כפל to the wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: [One who steals] the offspring of a wife's מלוג animal pays the double payment to the wife.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of רבי ינאי's ruling. A thief who steals the baby of an animal from the wife's מלוג property must pay the כפל, and that money goes to the wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With נכסי מלוג, the wife owns the property itself and the husband eats its פירות. Giving the כפל to the wife seems to treat the offspring as part of the wife's main property rather than as the husband's פירות. That is what the גמרא will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: A wife's property: she owns it, and the husband gets its produce
Double payment that a thief must pay

phrases.english: [One who steals] the offspring of a usufruct animal
phrases.notes: The words 'one who steals' come from the start of רבי ינאי's statement, just before this section begins.

phrases.english: pays the double payment to the woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלַד בֶּהֱמַת מְלוֹג מְשַׁלֵּם תַּשְׁלוּמֵי כֶפֶל לָאִשָּׁה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כפל for a stolen offspring of a מלוג animal goes to the wife.

steps.title: Whose opinion is this? Nobody's!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view רבי ינאי follows and claims it fits neither the רבנן nor חנניה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is not like the רבנן and not like חנניה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי ינאי's ruling. It says the ruling does not seem to match either side of a known מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כמאן' looks like a question, but here it works as an attack. The claim is that no known opinion would give the wife anything that comes from a מלוג animal's offspring. The source for this claim comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: חנניה, nephew of יאשיה, a תנא

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?
Not like the Rabbis and not like Ḥananya!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling in step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי's ruling that the כפל goes to the wife
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both opinions in the מחלוקת give the offspring of a מלוג animal to the husband, so the payment for it should go to him too.

steps.title: The ברייתא: animal offspring goes to the husband
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that the רבנן and חנניה both give the offspring of a מלוג animal to the husband. They argue only about a maidservant's child.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: the offspring of a מלוג animal belongs to the husband, and the child of a מלוג maidservant belongs to the wife. חנניה, son of יאשיה's brother, says: they made the child of a מלוג maidservant like the offspring of a מלוג animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up its challenge. The ברייתא shows that both views give animal offspring to the husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן split the cases: an animal's offspring goes to the husband, but a maidservant's child goes to the wife. חנניה treats the maidservant's child like the animal's offspring, so it also goes to the husband. Either way, an animal's offspring goes to the husband, so why should the wife get the כפל?

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught in a ברייתא
They (the Sages) made it, ruled it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the רבנן and חנניה argue about the animal. They agree the animal's offspring goes to the husband. They argue only about the maidservant's child.

phrases.english: As it was taught:
The offspring of a usufruct animal goes to the husband,
and the child of a usufruct maidservant goes to the wife.
And Ḥananya, son of Yoshiya's brother, said:
They made the child of a usufruct maidservant
like the offspring of a usufruct animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind the challenge in step 2
steps.raayaObject: The claim that both opinions give animal offspring to the husband
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא with the מחלוקת between the רבנן and חנניה

steps.title: Produce yes, produce of produce no
steps.stepSummary: Everyone can agree with רבי ינאי. The husband gets the פירות, but the כפל counts as פירא דפירא, which the Sages did not give him.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say this is everyone's view: the Sages gave him the produce, but they did not give him the produce of the produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי ינאי's ruling fits both opinions. The husband gets the offspring, but not the כפל that comes from stealing the offspring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The offspring is פירא, produce of the wife's animal, so it goes to the husband. The כפל is a further gain that came from that produce, so it is פירא דפירא. The Sages' enactment gave the husband only the first level of produce.

keyTerms.meaning: They enacted, set up as a rule

steps.whatToRemember: The husband's right in נכסי מלוג covers only פירא, not פירא דפירא. That is why the כפל for a stolen offspring goes to the wife.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a limit on how far the husband's rights in his wife's property reach.

phrases.english: You can even say it is the opinion of all:
the Rabbis instituted produce for him,

phrases.aramaic: פֵּירָא דְפֵירָא לָא תַּקִּינוּ לֵיה רַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: the produce of produce the Rabbis did not institute for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from steps 2 and 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the offspring is produce, while the כפל is produce of produce
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the offspring goes to the husband, the כפל for it should also go to him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The husband gets only first-level produce. The כפל is פירא דפירא, so it goes to the wife, and both opinions agree.

steps.title: Granted for חנניה: we don't worry about death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a new question. חנניה's view makes sense because we do not worry that the mother will die.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted according to חנניה: that is because we are not concerned about death.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. The גמרא says חנניה's view is easy to understand, and this prepares a question about the רבנן's view that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנניה treats the maidservant's child as produce for the husband because he does not worry that the mother will die. Since the mother is expected to stay as the wife's property, the child can be seen as produce. The word 'בשלמא' tells us a contrast is coming: the רבנן's view will be harder to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it makes sense (a challenge usually follows)

phrases.english: Granted, according to Ḥananya,
this is because we are not concerned about death.
phrases.notes: He means the mother might die. We don't worry about that, so the mother stays the main property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא from step 3 to start a new question about the reasoning behind each view
steps.kashyaTarget: The reasoning behind the רבנן's split between an animal and a maidservant (the question continues in the next lines)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Opens with 'בשלמא': חנניה's view is explained by not worrying about death. This sets up a question about how the רבנן's view works.

steps.title: The challenge to the Rabbis: why treat an animal and a maidservant differently?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the רבנן give a מלוג animal's offspring to the husband but a מלוג maidservant's child to the wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the רבנן: if they worry that the mother may die, then even the offspring of a מלוג animal should not go to the husband. And if they do not worry about death, then even the child of a מלוג maidservant should go to the husband too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the question it began in step 5. חנניה is consistent, but the רבנן seem to contradict themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason the רבנן give a maidservant's child to the wife is the worry that the maidservant could die and leave the wife with nothing. The child then replaces her. The same worry should apply to an animal, so treating the two cases differently looks inconsistent.

keyTerms.meaning: They are concerned about death (that the mother may die)
A maidservant belonging to the wife's מלוג property

phrases.english: But the Rabbis
if they are concerned about death
phrases.notes: He means the worry that the mother, the animal or the maidservant, might die and leave the wife with nothing.

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ וְלַד בֶּהֱמַת מְלוֹג נָמֵי לָא.
phrases.english: then even the offspring of a מלוג animal should also not [go to the husband].
And if they are not concerned about death
then even the child of a מלוג maidservant should also [go to the husband]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the question opened in step 5 by turning it against the רבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's split between a מלוג animal's offspring and a מלוג maidservant's child
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Inconsistency: the worry about the mother dying should apply to both cases or to neither.

steps.title: An animal is different because its hide remains
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן do worry about death, but a dead animal still leaves its hide, so the wife is not left with nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, they do worry about death. But an animal is different, because its hide is left over.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The רבנן really do worry that the mother might die, but an animal is a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a maidservant dies, nothing of value is left. If an animal dies, its hide still has value, so the wife's principal is not completely lost. That is why the offspring of an animal can go to the husband as produce.

phrases.english: Actually, they are concerned about death,
but an animal is different, since there is its hide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The worry about death should apply equally to an animal and a maidservant.
steps.terutzMaskana: The worry applies only where nothing remains. A dead animal leaves its hide, so the principal is not entirely lost.
steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן worry that the mother may die. A maidservant leaves nothing behind, so her child goes to the wife. An animal leaves its hide, so its offspring go to the husband.

steps.title: שמואל rules like חנניה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חייא reports in the name of שמואל that the הלכה follows חנניה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חייא said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה is like חנניה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives a practical ruling on the argument between the רבנן and חנניה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנניה holds that a מלוג maidservant's child goes to the husband, just like an animal's offspring. שמואל rules that this is the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who reports שמואל's ruling

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Ḥiyya said that Shmuel said:
The halakha is in accordance with Ḥananya.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הֲלָכָה כַּחֲנַנְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the logic of both views is explained, a practical ruling is given.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows חנניה: the child of a מלוג maidservant belongs to the husband.

steps.title: Even חנניה agrees a divorced wife may buy back the children
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן adds that if she is divorced, she may pay their value and take the maidservant's children, because of her family's honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב נחמן: even though שמואל ruled like חנניה, חנניה agrees that if she is divorced, she pays their value and takes them, because of the honor of her father's household.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן adds a limit to the ruling like חנניה for when the couple divorces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the marriage, the children belong to the husband. At divorce, the wife may pay him their value and take them. Her family's slaves should not stay with someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: The pride or honor of her father's household

phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Naḥman said:
Even though Shmuel said
the halakha is in accordance with Ḥananya,
Ḥananya concedes that if she was divorced,
she pays money and takes them,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the maidservant's children. She pays the husband what they are worth.

phrases.english: because of the pride of her father's household.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הֲלָכָה כַּחֲנַנְיָה, מוֹדֶה חֲנַנְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling of step 8 for the case of divorce.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At divorce, the wife may pay the value of her maidservant's children and take them, because of her family's honor.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows חנניה: the husband gets the maidservant's children. At divorce, though, the wife may buy them back for their value.

steps.title: Items brought in for their produce may be used until used up
steps.stepSummary: If she brought in a goat for milk, a sheep for wool, a hen for eggs, or a palm tree for fruit, the husband may keep taking the produce until the principal is used up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב נחמן: if she brought him a goat for its milk, a sheep for its wool, a hen for its eggs, or a palm tree for its fruit, he keeps eating until the principal is used up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new ruling about items the wife brings into the marriage for their produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These items were brought in for what they produce, so the husband keeps taking that produce. He does not have to stop to protect the principal, even though it will wear out over time.

keyTerms.meaning: She brought into the marriage for him
He continues to eat or use
The principal, the original item itself

phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Naḥman said:
If she brought in for him a goat for its milk,
or a sheep for its shearings,
or a hen for its eggs,
or a palm tree for its produce,
he continues to consume until the principal is consumed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling by רב נחמן about the husband's rights to produce of מלוג property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When an item is brought in for its produce, the husband may keep taking its produce until the item itself is used up.

steps.title: A cloak counts as produce and may be worn out
steps.stepSummary: If she brought in a cloak, it counts as produce, and he may wear it until it is worn out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: if she brought him a cloak, it counts as produce. He may cover himself with it until it is worn out.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a similar ruling about a cloak the wife brings into the marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wearing a cloak slowly uses it up. רב נחמן rules that this wearing counts as the husband's produce, so he may wear the cloak until nothing is left.

keyTerms.meaning: Until it is worn out or used up

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:
If she brought in for him a cloak,
it is produce,
and he may keep covering himself with it until it is used up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same idea as step 10 to a cloak.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cloak brought into the marriage counts as produce, so the husband may wear it until it is worn out.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב נחמן, when the wife brings in an item whose use naturally wears it down (a goat, sheep, hen, palm tree, or cloak), the husband may keep using it until it is gone.

steps.title: Whose view matches the cloak ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא agrees with רב נחמן's ruling that a cloak counts as produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the ruling just quoted, that a cloak counts as פירות. This sets up the next step, where it brings a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling a cloak 'produce' is surprising, because wearing it slowly uses up the cloak itself. So the גמרא wants to know which תנא holds that something which runs out over time can still count as פירות.

keyTerms.meaning: In accordance with whom? Whose view is this?

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?
phrases.notes: He means: whose view matches רב נחמן's ruling that a cloak counts as produce?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the cloak ruling in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that something which gets used up can still count as produce?

steps.title: The ברייתא on salt, sand and mines
steps.stepSummary: The ruling follows the חכמים in a ברייתא, who say that what is dug out of a sulfur pit or alum mine counts as produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows this תנא, as a ברייתא teaches: salt and sand count as produce. As for a sulfur pit or an alum mine, רבי מאיר says they are principal, and the חכמים say they are produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting a ברייתא. רב נחמן's cloak ruling matches the חכמים there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that salt and sand count as produce. A mine is different because it holds only a limited amount and will eventually run out. רבי מאיר therefore calls what is taken from it principal, while the חכמים still call it produce, which is the same reasoning as calling the cloak produce.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce or yield, which the husband may use
Principal, the asset itself, which stays the wife's

phrases.english: Like this תנא, as it is taught:
Salt and sand: this is produce.
phrases.notes: Picture the wife owning a piece of land where salt or sand is collected.

phrases.aramaic: פִּיר שֶׁל גׇּפְרִית, מַחְפּוֹרֶת שֶׁל צָרִיף,
phrases.english: A pit of sulfur, a mine of alum:
רבי מאיר says: it is principal.
And the חכמים say: it is produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by identifying the matching opinion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The cloak ruling follows the חכמים, who count material taken from a mine that will run out as produce.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that, according to the חכמים, something can count as produce even if taking it slowly uses up the source.

steps.title: Isn't רבי שמעון saying the same as the first תנא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון from the earlier משנה and asks how his view differs from the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: where his right is stronger, and so on. Isn't רבי שמעון saying the same thing as the first תנא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line from the earlier משנה. It asks why רבי שמעון's statement is needed if it seems to match what the first תנא already said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון said that where the husband's right is stronger when she enters the marriage, it is weaker when she leaves, and the reverse. That seems to repeat the first תנא's rules, so the גמרא wants to know what practical difference there is between them.

keyTerms.meaning: A case where his right is stronger
This is the same as the first תנא

phrases.english: רבי שמעון says:
Where his right is stronger.
phrases.notes: This is only the opening of רבי שמעון's line in the earlier משנה. It goes on to say his right is weaker when she leaves.

phrases.english: Isn't רבי שמעון the same as the first תנא?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by going back to the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the practical difference between רבי שמעון and the first תנא?

steps.title: רבא: they differ about crops still attached when she leaves
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the two views differ about produce that is still attached to the ground when the marriage ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the difference between them is produce that is still attached at the time she leaves.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by naming the case where the two views come out differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both views agree in the cases the משנה spelled out. They differ about crops still growing in the ground when the wife leaves the marriage. רבי שמעון's rule that his right is weaker when she leaves gives those crops to her, while according to the first תנא they belong to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Attached to the ground, meaning not yet harvested
At the time she leaves the marriage

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון is not just repeating the first תנא. They differ about crops still in the ground when the marriage ends.

phrases.english: רבא said:
Crops attached to the ground at the time she leaves
are the difference between them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They differ about crops still attached when she leaves. In רבי שמעון's view those go to her.

steps.title: משנה: old slaves the wife inherits
steps.stepSummary: If old slaves fall to her, they are sold and land is bought with the money. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says she does not have to sell them.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If old slaves and maidservants fell to her, they are sold, land is bought with the money, and he eats the produce. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: she need not sell them, because they are the pride of her father's house.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on old slaves the wife inherits, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Old slaves will soon be unable to work, so their value will disappear. The first תנא therefore turns them into land, which lasts, and the husband eats the produce of that land. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says they are the pride of her family, so she should not have to sell them.

keyTerms.meaning: Fell to her, meaning she inherited them
They are sold and land is bought
The pride of her father's house

phrases.english: משנה:
If old slaves and maidservants fell to her,
phrases.notes: She inherited them after the marriage.

phrases.english: they are sold, and land is bought with their value,
and he eats the produce.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: לֹא תִּמְכּוֹר,
phrases.english: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: she does not sell,
because they are the pride of her father's house.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ נָפְלוּ לָהּ עֲבָדִים וּשְׁפָחוֹת זְקֵנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Old slaves are sold and replaced with land, and the husband eats its produce. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: she need not sell them.

steps.title: משנה: old olive trees and vines
steps.stepSummary: The same ruling applies to old olive trees and vines, and here רבי יהודה disagrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: If old olive trees and vines fell to her, they are sold, land is bought with the money, and he eats the produce. רבי יהודה says: she need not sell them, because they are the pride of her father's house.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה repeats the same rule for old trees, with רבי יהודה taking the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Old trees give little fruit and will soon be finished, just like old slaves. So the first תנא again turns them into land that lasts. רבי יהודה uses the same family-pride reason as רבן שמעון בן גמליאל did for the slaves.

phrases.english: If old olive trees and vines fell to her,
they are sold, and land is bought with them,
and he eats the produce.
רבי יהודה says: she does not sell,
because they are the pride of her father's house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same rule as step 16 to trees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Old trees are sold and replaced with land. רבי יהודה: she need not sell them.

steps.title: רב: the argument is only about trees in her own field
steps.stepSummary: רב limits the disagreement about trees to trees in her own field. Trees in someone else's field must be sold according to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב כהנא said in the name of רב: the argument is when they fell to her in her own field. But in a field that is not hers, everyone agrees she sells them, because the principal is being used up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רב explaining exactly where רבי יהודה's argument applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the trees stand in her own field, they are part of her family's estate, so רבי יהודה lets her keep them. If she owns only the trees in someone else's field, there is nothing lasting to keep, since the trees will die out. So everyone agrees she must sell them.

keyTerms.meaning: The principal is being used up

steps.confusionAlert: רב is only limiting the case of the trees. He is not saying anything about the slaves.

phrases.english: גמרא:
רב כהנא said that רב said:
The argument is where they fell to her in her own field,
phrases.notes: "They" means the old olive trees and vines.

phrases.english: but in a field that is not hers,
everyone agrees she sells them,
because the principal is being used up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר רַב: מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the disagreement in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is only about trees in her own field. In someone else's field, everyone agrees the trees are sold.
steps.whyThisMatters: This first version of רב's statement ties the family-pride reason to something lasting staying in the family. רב יוסף challenges this version in the next step, and the גמרא then reverses it.

steps.title: רב יוסף challenges רב's limit on the dispute
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף points out that old slaves are just like a field that is not hers, yet the תנאים still disagree about them. So רב's limit does not fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objects: Old slaves and maidservants are like a field that is not hers, and the תנאים still disagree about them!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks רב's statement from Step 18. That statement said only trees in her own field are in dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said everyone agrees trees in someone else's field must be sold, because nothing of the principal will remain. But old slaves will also die and leave nothing, so they are like a field that is not hers. Still, the תנא קמא and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagree about them. So 'not hers' cannot mean everyone agrees.

keyTerms.meaning: Objects to it; raises a strong challenge

phrases.english: Rav Yosef objects to this:
But slaves and maidservants
phrases.notes: He means the old slaves from Step 16, who will die and leave nothing behind.

phrases.english: are like a field that is not hers,
and yet they disagree!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's limit from Step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that everyone agrees trees in a field that is not hers must be sold
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Old slaves also leave no lasting principal, yet the תנאים disagree about them. So 'nothing remains' does not make everyone agree.

steps.title: The גמרא flips רב's statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא restates רב the other way around. The dispute is about trees in a field that is not hers. In her own field, everyone agrees she does not sell, because of her family's honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, it was said like this: רב כהנא said in the name of רב: The dispute is about a field that is not hers. But in her own field, everyone agrees she does not sell, because of the pride of her father's house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the old version of רב's statement and gives a corrected version that avoids רב יוסף's problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the field that is not hers is the place of the dispute. This matches the slaves case, where nothing lasting remains and they still disagree. In her own field, the trees are part of her family's land, so the reason of שבח בית אביה is strong enough that even the תנא קמא agrees she does not have to sell them.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, this is how it was said (a corrected version)
The pride or honor of her father's house

steps.confusionAlert: This is the exact opposite of Step 18. There, the field that is not hers was where everyone agreed. Here, it is where they argue.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was said, it was said like this:
Rav Kahana said that Rav said:
The dispute is about a field that is not hers,
but in her own field
everyone agrees she does not sell,
because of the pride of her father's house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge by reversing רב's statement
steps.terutzResolutionType: Restating the earlier statement in reverse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute was only about trees in her own field
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute is about trees in a field that is not hers. In her own field, everyone agrees she keeps them because of family honor.
steps.whatToRemember: Final version: trees in someone else's field are in dispute. Trees in her own field are not sold, according to everyone, because of שבח בית אביה.

steps.title: New משנה: a husband's spending on his wife's property
steps.stepSummary: A husband who spent money improving his wife's property and also ate some of its produce does not settle accounts, no matter the amounts. If he ate nothing, he swears how much he spent and takes it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who spends money on his wife's property: if he spent a lot and ate a little, or spent a little and ate a lot, what he spent he spent, and what he ate he ate. If he spent and did not eat, he swears how much he spent and takes it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It deals with a husband who invested in his wife's property and then the marriage ended.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he ate any produce at all, nobody pays anybody back, even if the amounts are very uneven. Only if he ate nothing can he claim his spending back, and he must take an oath about the amount.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One who spends money on his wife's property,
if he spent a lot and ate a little,
or spent a little and ate a lot,
what he spent he spent,
and what he ate he ate.
If he spent and did not eat,
he swears how much he spent, and takes it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמּוֹצִיא הוֹצָאוֹת עַל נִכְסֵי אִשְׁתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If he ate any produce, there is no reckoning. If he ate none, he swears to his expenses and collects them.

steps.title: How much is 'a little'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the smallest amount of eating is that counts as 'a little'.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: And how much is 'a little'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks to define the משנה's word קימעא. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating even 'a little' stops the husband from claiming his expenses. So it matters a lot where the lower limit is.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גְּמָרָא, the גמרא's discussion

phrases.english: Gemara:
And how much is "a little"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to define a word in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum amount of eating that counts as קימעא

steps.title: רבי אסי: even one dried fig
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי says even one dried fig counts, as long as he ate it in a dignified way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said: Even one dried fig, provided he ate it in a dignified way. It was said...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי answers the question. Even a tiny amount of eating counts, if it was eaten properly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The amount can be tiny, but the way he ate matters. It has to be eaten respectfully, like an owner eating his produce, and not grabbed in a hurry. The last word starts a new statement that continues later.

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said:
even one dried fig,
provided that he ate it in a dignified way.
It was said...

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אֲפִילּוּ גְּרוֹגֶרֶת אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 22
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even one dried fig counts as 'a little', if it was eaten in a dignified way
